questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to study in an English-speaking country that offered exciting opportunities to experience both nature and culture. I have always wanted to visit Australia, and because it is so far away from Denmark, I saw the exchange as a unique and once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to live there for half a year.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was not difficult to find the required information upon arrival. However, the process is quite long and involves many deadlines that need to be met. I would therefore strongly recommend creating a clear overview of all important deadlines and ensuring that the necessary documents are prepared in advance. Despite the length of the process, it is absolutely worth it in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had organized an orientation week upon arrival. This included a mandatory introductory session as well as a variety of social activities, such as a campus tour, tastings of Australian specialties, and speed-friending events. I did not know anyone before arriving, and although it was sometimes a bit outside my comfort zone, I made an effort to participate in many of the activities at the beginning. This turned out to be a great way to build a network early on while being far from home, as everyone is eager to meet new people.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
For me, finding accommodation was not particularly difficult. I created a profile on an app called Flatmates, where people looking for a flatmate can connect with potential tenants and vice versa. I wanted to have my housing arranged before arriving, so I had an online meeting with my landlord, who showed me the room virtually. This ended up being the room I moved into.

However, I would advise others to be cautious. Before signing with my landlord, I had considered another room that looked very nice in the pictures. Fortunately, my boyfriend’s brother, who lives in Sydney, was able to view the room on my behalf. It turned out to be in very poor condition, and I was relieved that I had someone who could check it in person. If possible, I would therefore recommend waiting to secure accommodation until after arrival, so you can see the place yourself, as there is a risk of scams.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in Sydney is expensive, and many shared houses have installed video surveillance in common areas. I lived in a house with surveillance, which I did not find particularly comfortable. I was aware of this before moving in, but I was quite desperate to secure accommodation at the time. In hindsight, I wish I had waited, as it turned out that finding a place to live was not as difficult as I initially expected.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process was generally straightforward. Before course registration opened, I had already decided which courses I wanted to enroll in, which I would strongly recommend, as UTS operates on a first-come, first-served basis. I therefore set an alarm in the middle of the night when registration opened to ensure that I secured my preferred courses.

Registration was completed through an online system where students could select courses from a list of available options. The system also provided detailed timetables for each course, making it possible to choose specific class times. Many students aimed to concentrate their classes into as few days on campus as possible, allowing for greater flexibility during the week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UTS had provided a course catalogue with pre-approved courses that all exchange students could choose from without any issues. There was a wide selection of courses available, and many of them aligned well with my degree program.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is important to be aware of which courses you want and to be prepared when registration opens for enrollment.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, I found the academic level at KU to be somewhat higher than at UTS. However, I was surprised by the continuous assessment structure at UTS, as there were many assignments throughout the semester. Grading is handled differently, with each assignment or presentation contributing a specific percentage to the final grade. For example, in one course I had two major written assignments during the semester, each accounting for 35% of the final grade, followed by an oral exam worth the remaining 30%. This structure required consistent effort throughout the semester rather than focusing solely on a final exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
All of our lectures were held online, and many of them were pre-recorded. Personally, I prefer in-person teaching; however, the pre-recorded lectures offered a high degree of flexibility, as long as they were watched before the scheduled tutorials. This allowed students to engage with the material at a time that suited them best.

Overall, the tutorial sessions were largely comparable to those at KU, although the level of preparation among tutors varied considerably. In several of my courses, attendance at tutorials was mandatory and absences were recorded, with only two absences permitted throughout the semester. In one of my courses, 20% of the final grade was based on active participation, which encouraged all students to contribute actively to class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Project Management
Career and Portfolio Planning
Event Creation Workshop

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Career and Portfolio Planning was a very valuable and useful course. As I am currently pursuing my Master’s degree and will soon be entering the job market, the course encouraged meaningful self-reflection by focusing on identifying professional strengths as well as areas for improvement. The final oral examination was designed as a simulated job interview, which made the course particularly relevant and practical.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was surprised by how expensive it was to live in Sydney. I lived in a shared house with 11 other people and paid over DKK 7,000 per month for a single room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The visa for Australia is very expensive. I paid over DKK 7,000 for my visa. In addition, traveling within Australia is very expensive. I would therefore recommend allocating sufficient time before departure to apply for scholarships and to travel with some personal savings.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many different student organizations and clubs available; however, I was not actively involved in any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide range of student clubs and societies, including surfing, running, tennis, dance, martial arts, hiking, camping, women in Business, theatre, IT clubs, and there even was a society for swifties. During the orientation week, there was a dedicated day where students could walk around and learn more about the different clubs. There was something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Coastal walks, blue mountains, surf-camp, visiting the opera house, and generally just travelling around Australia, there are so many nice places to visit.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Uluru! It is located in the middle of Australia, and I have never seen anything like it. We slept in swags, which are a type of sleeping bag, and it was one of the greatest experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter many cultural differences that I found challenging. The biggest challenge was probably establishing a daily routine in a new country, but even that became manageable relatively quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed lifestyle and how open and chill Australians are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to set aside plenty of time to apply for scholarships before departure.
2. Be active in the social events organized by the university at the beginning, as they are a great way to build a strong network.
3. Travel – there are so many exciting places to explore in Australia!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Going on exchange requires a significant amount of work, especially before departure, but it is all worth it in the end.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I went on some incredible trips with the most wonderful people I met during my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference can be challenging when you have family, friends, and a partner back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
